title: Mumbai's FDA Crackdown Reaches Elite Clubs and Street Eateries Alike
excerpt: Maharashtra's food safety chief Tukaram Mundhe has suspended licences at establishments ranging from the Cricket Club of India to Bhendi Bazaar restaurants, expanding a drive that has now hit Domino's, quick-commerce warehouses, and hundreds of food businesses statewide.
body:
• Maharashtra's FDA has suspended food licences at five elite Mumbai clubs — including the Cricket Club of India and Willingdon Sports Club — after inspectors found cockroach infestations, expired food, and rotten vegetables in kitchens.
  • The crackdown has expanded to cover restaurants in Bhendi Bazaar and Umarkhadi, four Domino's outlets, and 12 quick-commerce warehouses belonging to Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy's Instamart.
  • FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has inspected 86 establishments in recent rounds alone, issuing 60 improvement notices and seizing prohibited products worth lakhs of rupees.
  • The enforcement drive, described by Reuters as historically unprecedented in scope, has drawn widespread public support and intensified scrutiny of India's food service industry.

From Elite Clubs to Street Kitchens

Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration has suspended the FSSAI licences of five of Mumbai's most prestigious private clubs after surprise inspections between July 24 and 27 uncovered serious food safety violations, according to the FDA's official statement reported by Press Trust of India.

The suspended establishments include the Cricket Club of India, MIG Cricket Club, RK Juhu Gymkhana, The Aparna Juhu Gymkhana, and The Willingdon Sports Club. At the Cricket Club of India, inspectors found cockroaches and flies inside food preparation areas, rotten vegetables, overripe mushrooms, expired food items, and water leaking into cold storage units, according to the FDA inspection report cited by ET Legal World.

The kitchen had failed to follow FIFO (First In, First Out) and FEFO (First Expired, First Out) inventory practices, and vegetarian and non-vegetarian food preparation areas were not adequately segregated, raising cross-contamination concerns.

The Bureaucrat Behind the Campaign

The enforcement drive is led by FDA Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, 51, who has made food safety his signature issue since taking charge of Maharashtra's food regulatory apparatus. Reports of contamination are common in India's food sector, Reuters noted, but Mundhe's approach has gathered unprecedented public and media attention for its rigour — targeting establishments regardless of reputation or stature.

"We will not tolerate any playing with public health."

— Tukaram Mundhe, FDA Commissioner, Maharashtra

In a single recent round, the FDA inspected 86 establishments statewide, issued 60 improvement notices, and suspended permits at multiple locations. Between June 26 and 28 alone, the agency conducted 31 inspections across Maharashtra, seizing prohibited food items — including pan masala and gutkha — worth Rs 34.87 lakh and arresting 19 people in connection with banned food products, according to the FDA's official statement.

The Scope Keeps Growing

The crackdown has expanded far beyond clubs. In Bhendi Bazaar and Umarkhadi, the FDA suspended licences of three restaurants after inspections uncovered wet and slippery kitchen floors, missing procurement records, no documentation of drinking water quality, improper segregation of vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, and open windows without insect-proof screens, The Times of India reported.

The FDA this month also shut four Domino's outlets — a brand typically considered to maintain stricter safety protocols — and suspended permits at 12 quick-commerce warehouses belonging to Eternal's Blinkit, Zepto, and Swiggy's Instamart. Photos shared by the FDA showed rusted storage racks with cockroaches crawling around food items at warehouse facilities.

At MIG Cricket Club, inspectors found an unlicensed catering operation — Nebula Catering Services — running without a valid FSSAI licence, alongside pest infestations, missing food and water testing records, and unauthorised structural modifications. The remaining clubs were cited for poor sanitation, deteriorating kitchen infrastructure, and non-compliance with mandatory food safety standards.

A $13 Billion Sector Under Scrutiny

The raids on quick-commerce warehouses put a spotlight on India's $13 billion rapid delivery sector. Swiggy and Zepto operate roughly 1,100 delivery outlets each, while Blinkit runs approximately 2,200, according to Datum Intelligence. At a Zepto warehouse in Nashik, delivery staff were entering storage areas in street footwear, creating cross-contamination risks.

Consumer response on social media has been overwhelmingly supportive. "About damn time. A city-wide crackdown in all quick e-commerce warehouses is needed," one user wrote on X, capturing a widespread sentiment that enforcement has historically been absent in India's food service industry.

What It Means for Diaspora Visitors

For NRIs visiting Mumbai, the crackdown offers both reassurance and caution. The enforcement drive signals a shift toward accountability in food safety — but the sheer volume of violations discovered suggests that problems extend well beyond the establishments that have been inspected so far.

All suspended establishments must rectify deficiencies and demonstrate compliance with the Food Safety and Standards Act before their licences can be reinstated. The enforcement drive continues, with Mundhe's office signalling that no category of food business is exempt from scrutiny.
image_caption: Mumbai's Food and Drug Administration has intensified inspections across the city, targeting elite clubs and street eateries alike for food safety violations.
nri_angle: NRIs visiting Mumbai should note the widespread hygiene violations found even at elite establishments, though the enforcement drive signals improving accountability.
